text:
ana: heads up — saw a persistent divergence between canary and baseline on /v1/generate for model-x in eu-west yesterday evening. canary error-rate ~2.1% vs baseline 0.3% for the same window :thinking:

mike: ugh, did we change any routing or quantization for that canary?

sophia: no infra changes that I know of. rollout was just a traffic bump from 2% -> 10% at 18:04 UTC.

ana: (typo) ana: i grabbed the slice: errors are concentrated on requests with long contexts (>2k tokens) and with streaming enabled.

jordan: can you paste the query you used? want to reproduce in the dashboard.

ana: sure, quick timeseries I ran in observability:
```sql
SELECT timestamp_bin(1m, ts) as t, count(*) as total, sum(case when status >= 500 then 1 else 0 end) as errors
FROM requests
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND model = 'model-x' AND region = 'eu-west'
GROUP BY t ORDER BY t
```

mike: looks like the guard fired and rerouted some traffic to baseline after 18:22, but the initial spike lasted ~8m. deploy-bot: can you confirm the guard logs?

deploy-bot: traffic-guard: canary=10% -> fallback at 18:22 UTC due to error-rate threshold 1.0% exceeded. reason: "rate(500) > 1.0%".

pranay: hmm threshold 1% seems aggressive for high-variance slices. maybe the guard should be per-slice (context-length bucket) not global.

lia: agree — if 90% of errors come from the 2k+ bucket and that bucket is only 4% of traffic, global thresholds are noisy. propose: add slice-aware guard that computes a rolling p99 and trimmed-mean error across slices and only trips if both overall and top-affected-slice exceed limits.

mike: UX implication: console currently only shows global canary vs baseline metrics. need a drilldown that surfaces top-10 slices by delta with a small sample link. e.g. "View 100 sample requests" that opens anonymized request+response for quick triage.

sophia: sketch of proposed guard logic:
```text
- compute per-slice error_rate over last 5m
- compute global weighted_error = sum(slice_error * slice_weight)
- compute trim_mean = median of slice_errors excluding top/bottom 10%
- trip guard if weighted_error > global_threshold AND trim_mean > trim_threshold
```

jordan: +1. Also add hysteresis: require 2 consecutive 1m windows above threshold before fallback. reduced flapping.

ana: question: how do we pick slice keys? suggested: (model_variant, region, context_len_bucket, streaming_enabled) — should be configurable per rollout.

pranay: yes make keys configurable. default to model_variant+region and an optional dimension picker in the rollout modal.

lia: alerting change: for canaries we should send an "insight" to the rollout channel with top 3 slices and quick links, not just a global incident. also include sample query to reproduce.

mike: engineering asks: can we get a backfill of the last 48h for the 2k+ bucket to see if this is recurring? sophia, can infra expose sample table?

sophia: yep, I can add a job that materializes per-slice 1m aggregates to the metrics store for 48h. will do tomorrow AM.

ana: temporary mitigation — reduce canary ramp to 1% and enable per-slice guard. I'll open a tiny rollback PR now.

mike: pls include a note in the rollout page that context-length slices may trigger false positives. tied to ops runbook.

ana: done — PR #482 includes guard config + description. linking: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/12345

pranay: next steps (summarized):
- sophia: materialize slice aggregates (48h)
- eng-platform: implement slice-aware guard + hysteresis
- console: add "View sample" drilldown + top-slices card
- ops: update runbook to look at context_len slice first

mike: sounds good. tagging @sophia @lia for console/ux sync tomorrow. :eyes:

deploy-bot: note: fallback executed at 18:22 UTC. canary traffic restored to baseline at 18:23 UTC after automatic rollback window.

ana: thanks all, will monitor post-change and report back with backfill results.

sophia: thanks — will post a follow-up thread with the materialized view once available.

mike: appreciate the quick triage team :thumbsup:
